headline: Man held for 'sniper' comment on PM's bus during Rajshahi visit
summary: Detectives have detained Abu Bokor Siddique from Rajshahi after he posted a Facebook comment suggesting a sniper could have targeted a university bus carrying Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. He is being brought to Dhaka for questioning.
details: Detectives have detained a young man in Rajshahi for a Facebook comment suggesting a sniper could have targeted a university bus carrying Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. The comment, which spread across social media, was deemed an 'outrageous threat' by police.

The suspect, identified as Abu Bokor Siddique, was picked up by a team from the Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s (DMP) Detective Branch. He is currently being brought to the capital for questioning with assistance from the Special Response Battalion (SRB).

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman visited Rajshahi on Tuesday, arriving at Shah Makhdum Airport. He then entered the city in a bus from the Rajshahi University of Engineering and Technology (RUET), waving to crowds lining the roads.

A Facebook page, 'The Beauty of Rajshahi,' posted about the use of the RUET bus, questioning why the prime minister's usual bulletproof vehicle was not used. It was on this post that Abu Bokor Siddique's account commented: 'What a golden chance. All that was missing was a sniper.'

Rajshahi Metropolitan Police spokesperson Gaziur Rahman confirmed on Wednesday that the commenter had been identified and legal action was initiated. Details regarding any formal inquiry into the comment's threat level are not yet available.

headline: Over 2,300 tourists stranded in Sajek amid blockade
summary: Protesters have blocked the road to Sajek Valley, leaving hundreds of vehicles and thousands of tourists stuck near Ujo Bazar.
details: Approximately 2,350 tourists in about 450 vehicles are stranded near Ujo Bazar in Rangamati's Baghaichari Upazila after protesters blocked the road with tree trunks.
The blockade was called by the Sajek Karbari Association and the Sajek Gono Odhikar Rokkha Committee, who have launched an indefinite protest.
Sajek Gono Odhikar Rokkha Committee President Babudhan Chakma stated that the blockade is peaceful but no vehicles, including tourist vehicles, will be allowed to pass.
The tourist convoy, which left Sajek around 8:30 am on Thursday, was stopped 25km from the valley when they reached the Ujo Bazar area.
Sajek Police Station chief Md Hossain confirmed that law enforcement agencies are currently negotiating with the protesters to safely transport the tourists to their destinations.
The district administration has also imposed a temporary ban on tourist travel to the valley starting from Wednesday evening due to the ongoing blockade.

Sajek Gono Odhikar Rokkha Committee President Babudhan Chakma stated that the blockade is peaceful but no vehicles, including tourist vehicles, will be allowed to pass.

The tourist convoy, which left Sajek around 8:30 am on Thursday, was stopped 25km from the valley when they reached the Ujo Bazar area.

Sajek Police Station chief Md Hossain confirmed that law enforcement agencies are currently negotiating with the protesters to safely transport the tourists to their destinations.
